title: Derived interpretation of the integral pulled quotient Roos augmentation
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. On the small pro-étale sites put $C_Z=(A)_Z$, $R_Z=\mathcal O_{E,Z}$ and $S_{n,Z}=(A/\pi^n)_Z$ for $Z=X,Y$, $n\geq1$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Write $i_Z:C_Z\to R_Z$ for the constant-function map, $r_Z=\operatorname{Res}_{i_Z}$ for scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and $g_R^*,g_C^*$ for module pullback along the canonical coefficient maps [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback, sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms].

Let $P$ be a flat-term K-flat complex of $R_Y$-modules, put $Q=r_YP$, and form the augmented strict quotient towers
$$T_n=g_R^*(P\otimes_{R_Y}S_{n,Y}),\quad U_n=g_R^*P\otimes_{R_X}S_{n,X},\quad V_n=g_C^*(Q\otimes_{C_Y}S_{n,Y})$$
[def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Use unbounded derived categories with localization $\mathsf q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define $\mathsf R(W)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_nW_n\to\prod_nW_n)[-1]$ with differential $D(y,x)=(-dy-(1-s)x,dx)$ and $\alpha_W(z)=(0,(b_{W,n}z)_n)$ for its quotient augmentation. Let $\rho_W:\mathsf q\mathsf R(W)\cong R\!\lim W$ be the comparison normalized on a K-injective tower by the inclusion $z\mapsto(0,(z_n)_n)$ [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison].

Under $R_Z\cong\varprojlim_n S_{n,Z}$, the coefficient map $c_g:g^{-1}\varprojlim_nS_{n,Y}\to\varprojlim_nS_{n,X}$ defined by finite projections [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] equals the canonical Cartesian coefficient isomorphism $a_R:g^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$. In particular, for every $n$,
$$\mathrm{pr}_{n,X}a_R=a_{n}\,g^{-1}\mathrm{pr}_{n,Y},\qquad a_n:g^{-1}S_{n,Y}\cong S_{n,X}.$$
In the derived category of strict $R_X$-towers, the complex $T$ with its augmentation represents $Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}(\mathsf q(P\otimes_{R_Y}S_{n,Y}))_n$ together with the derived pulled quotient augmentation. In the respective derived tower categories, $U$ and $V$ represent the finite derived reduction towers of $Lg_R^*[P]$ and $Lg_C^*[Q]$; the identification for $V$ is the generator-normalized constant tensor-pullback comparison.

There are natural derived isomorphisms $\mathsf q\mathsf R(U)\cong (Lg_R^*[P])^\wedge$ in $D(R_X)$ and $\mathsf q\mathsf R(V)\cong (Lg_C^*[Q])^\wedge$ in $D(C_X)$, carrying $\mathsf q\alpha_U$ and $\mathsf q\alpha_V$ to the respective actual derived-completion units. Also $\rho_T\mathsf q\alpha_T$ is the augmented strict-derived-tower map obtained by the constant-tower unit followed by derived inverse limit of the pulled quotient augmentation. On derived-complete inputs this is the comparison of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. On derived-complete inputs, the scalar-restricted construction is precisely constant-coefficient completed inverse image; on arbitrary inputs the same formula is ordinary inverse image followed by derived completion with its unit [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. These identifications retain the distinction between $D(R_X)$ and $D(C_X)$ and impose no boundedness, constructibility or completeness condition on $[P]$.

proof.text: Both coefficient maps into the completed ring have equal finite projections. The limit universal property gives equality; projection_comm gives the displayed finite squares.

Choose the normalized strict cone representatives and their derived-limit comparisons, independently of the parent strict normalization theorem. Obtain preservation of the flat K-flat class and the four counit isomorphisms. Localize the augmentations by their coordinate normalization.

Apply the descent theorem to the fixed chain comparisons and the localized unit equations, using the resolving counits for its invertibility hypotheses. It supplies the natural completion isomorphisms and their unit identities. Assemble them with the chosen chain data, resolving predicates, four counit isomorphisms and the localized completed-pullback equation.
